decisions.reason: The posting cadence and time window do not change which clips may be published, their destination, or their Reel format; the same-message format change is already represented.
The schedule change does not alter the required caption, hashtags, tagged account, or tag placement.
Publishing one clip per day during peak hours does not change the requirement to update each corresponding Notion card after posting.
The source continues to use the assigned Instagram account but does not change its creation, profile, or audience-routing requirements.
The posting schedule does not change which published clips are tracked or the tracked performance metrics.
The approved clips being scheduled for publication are not shown to modify the already completed initial three-clip trial.
The source confirms that the current clips passed the existing approval gate but does not change the approval authority, eligibility rule, or correction policy.
The publication cadence for three approved clips does not modify the earlier task-local requirement to create one reference-matching requalification clip.
Instructions to publish this batch as Instagram Reels do not necessarily remove or change the broader editing targets of Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok.
The posting cadence and time window do not change the permitted source videos or moment-selection criteria.
The source provides publishing instructions without changing the required 45-to-60-second clip duration.
The live-posting schedule does not change the earlier Google Drive delivery package or its audit submission details.
